chunks: And from him, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Isa ibn Abdullah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the testimony of the child of fornication, so he said: 'It is not valid except in small matters, if you see goodness in him.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a child of fornication accepted in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a nuanced ruling for walad al-zina, accepting their testimony in minor legal matters if moral rectitude (salah) is observed, thereby balancing the stigma of lineage with individual merit. This view reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the potential for purification of the individual despite the father's sin, distinguishing between the defect in lineage and the integrity of the witness. It underscores the principle that legal capacity is not permanently barred by birth circumstances but is contingent upon demonstrated piety.
